summary: Refines the existing P0-A shared-service lifecycle authority after a read-only bootstrap audit found three pre-deployment contract gaps: missing-state reads wrote lock files, rollback worker imports incorrectly followed the old physical target, and the worker did not re-verify target bytes immediately before effect.

components.disposition: ADMIT as a narrow refinement of the existing P0-A authority: make read-only desired-state observation physically zero-write, keep detached controller import identity on current control code during rollback, and re-verify desired physical target bytes under the lifecycle lease before invoking any old/new restart script.
evidence: Temporary missing-state audit mechanically reproduced read=None followed by creation of service-control-state.lock.
A pre-P0-A temporary target without the service_control module left the detached action nonterminal because the worker imported from the desired target root.
A clean published temporary target modified after acceptance was previously executed successfully; P0-A.1 now durable-fails before the script when exact binding verification detects drift.
The existing lifecycle lease remains the publication-vs-effect serialization authority; no second restart executor or semantic policy is introduced.
components.verification_level: deterministic RED/GREEN, 53-test focused matrix, 191-test adjacency, runtime-env ratchet, Ruff/Pyright, whole-tree security, and full repository ci_gate
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: The model still receives desired generation/action terminal/binding evidence and decides whether restart or rollback is useful. Missing desired state is observable without side effects; a stale or byte-drifted target fails before physical execution; rollback may target pre-P0-A code because controller and physical target identity are explicit separate facts.
components.rollback_route: Revert this follow-up to P0-A code with no application-data migration. Operational service rollback while P0-A.1 is active remains a monotonic new desired generation pointing at the prior qualified physical target, while preserving the current controller code root until the action terminal receipt.

g1.necessity: P0-A cannot be safely bootstrapped while documented read-only status mutates lock state, rollback workers cannot import when the desired target predates service_control, and accepted targets can drift after publication yet still execute through old scripts. These are mechanical correctness gaps in the already-approved lifecycle authority.

g2.authority_owner: existing P0-A generation-bound shared-service lifecycle control plane
g2.non_duplication: P0-A.1 creates no second service-control authority and no second physical restart path. It reuses the same desired deployment, action receipts, lifecycle lease, binding verifier, and restart_mirror execution plan, while correcting read semantics and controller-vs-target identity.

binding failure detail before physical script execution

g3.recovery_or_reason: Missing state remains observable without creating control files. A rollback can use a pre-P0-A target because the detached controller remains on current control code. If target roots/head/clean/artifact identity change after publish/accept, the worker durable-fails before effect, allowing the model/operator to republish a new generation or choose another target.

g4.rollback: No application-data migration is introduced. Revert P0-A.1 to P0-A source if necessary. For operational service rollback under P0-A.1, publish the prior qualified physical target as the next generation, retain the current controller root until terminal receipt, then validate the restarted target normally.
